questions.tag: United States of America · Central bank policy
questions.q: Why did the Federal Reserve raise interest rates?
o: To counter persistent inflation and elevated energy costs
To boost the valuation of newly listed Nasdaq stocks
To weaken the United States dollar against the Japanese yen
To support foreign exchange liquidity in developing markets
questions.e: The Federal Reserve tightened monetary policy by raising borrowing costs in response to stubborn price pressures and high energy prints. Higher rates act as a brake on economic activity when inflation is elevated. The other choices misidentify the primary driver, which was domestic price growth rather than equity listings or exchange rates.

questions.q: What action did the Bank of England take regarding its quantitative tightening schedule?

It increased benchmark interest rates to match the United States Federal Reserve

questions.e: The Bank of England held its benchmark rate steady and simultaneously altered its quantitative tightening plan by reducing gilts sales. This operational shift slowed the pace of portfolio runoff. The other options either reverse the direction of the gilts adjustment or incorrectly claim a rate change.
